text:
Alice Chen: Quick help — customer (InfoSec lead) asked for our exact breach notification timeline and what we share during a POC. Need a short script I can send.

Raj Patel: Short version: we follow applicable legal/regulatory timelines (GDPR 72h, etc.) and our contractual obligations. Operationally we escalate immediately, investigate, and notify customers as soon as we confirm a material impact. Typical customer-facing timeline: initial triage within 24–48h of confirmation and status updates every 24h until resolution. Formal written notice per contract/regulator.

Ben Li: For Redwood Dedicated/Private: customer-managed network boundaries often mean the customer controls some aspects of containment. We will still assist with forensics and remediation and will notify if our service caused the exposure or we detect tenant data exfil. We coordinate directly with the customer's IR lead.

Raj Patel: Our IR flow: Detect → Triage (severity) → Contain → Eradicate → Recover → Notify. Internal trigger: any confirmed data exfil or tenant-impacting incident triggers CISO + Legal + SRE + Sales notification. We preserve chain-of-custody: logs, snapshots, and evidence stored per our forensics playbook.

ir-bot: Incident created: IR-2025-142 assigned to oncall. (auto-note)

Dan O'Neill: Legal note — do not promise precise language without Legal sign-off. Suggested customer-safe phrasing: 'We take security seriously. Upon confirmation of a security incident affecting your data we will notify your designated security contact promptly and follow applicable legal and regulatory timelines (e.g., GDPR — no later than 72 hours).' Refer to the MSA for formal notification timing.

Maria Gomez: Also call out what we provide: timeline of events, scope (which tenant/keys/snapshots affected), indicators of compromise (IOCs), mitigations applied, recommended next steps, and a named IR contact. We can provide redacted logs/forensics under NDA.

Ben Li: Operationally we aim to: initial customer-facing triage within 24h of confirmation; interim updates every 24h; final technical incident report within 7–14 business days depending on complexity. If they need SOC 2 / ISO evidence we can attach control evidence and timelines.

Raj Patel: For GDPR customers we explicitly say 'as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after becoming aware' — clarify that 'becoming aware' = when we have reasonable evidence of a breach (not unverified rumors). Also confirm the customer's preferred SIR/SOC contact channel so we send notifications to the right inbox.

Alice Chen: Can you drop a one-paragraph email I can send to the customer? Keep it short — I'll loop in Legal if needed.

Raj Patel: Sure — paste below:

```
Hi <Name>,

Short answer: Upon confirmation of a security incident affecting your data we will notify your designated security contact promptly and follow applicable legal and regulatory timelines (for example, GDPR — no later than 72 hours after becoming aware). Operationally we provide an initial triage within 24–48 hours of confirmation, regular status updates, and a final technical incident report. We will share scope, indicators, mitigations taken, and recommended next steps, and we will coordinate directly with your IR lead. For Dedicated/Private deployments we will work closely with your team to preserve evidence and assist with remediation.

IR contact: security@redwood.com | Legal: legal@redwood.com

Regards,
Raj Patel
```

Dan O'Neill: LGTM; tweak to add 'subject to legal/regulatory obligations and non-disclosure' in the email before sending.

Alice Chen: Great — will add the legal sentence and send. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
